The finite Mobius identity (verified exactly) yields the claimed uniform d<b error, and the d>=b tail completes the total-variation estimate. All quantifiers, endpoints and normalization were reviewed; the exact verifier passed 496 local laws and 3500 symbolic checks. The computation is diagnostic, not a substitute for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The two coupled floor polynomials differ by the rational linear polynomial n/b, and hence violate the published total homogeneous equidistribution condition. The published single-floor result already covers b=1, but none of the inspected full statements yields the complete b-dependent gcd mass function, the exact d>=b zeta-two tail, and the quantitative total-variation interpolation. The closest full published research records treat an integer polynomial times independently equidistributed floor coordinates, or a purely rational two-coordinate floor dilation, neither of which implies the dependent three-coordinate result. Multiple targeted research searches found no equivalent statement; this is evidence for novelty rather than a proof of historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: A natural test of the polynomial-gcd coprimality theorem precisely at a rank-deficient, rationally coupled floor-vector boundary. The result gives a complete, normalized distribution rather than an arbitrary small example, identifies a sharp arithmetic cutoff d=b beyond which the two-variable heavy tail is exact, and proves quantitative total-variation recovery of the independent three-variable law. It has a clear structural role in distinguishing correlation from equidistribution.
